My biggest three complaints with the game:

  1. Ammo should be craftable. It really burns my ass that my character can make extensive modifications to laser rifles and power armor, but can't recharge a single damn fusion cell despite having hand-built a working power station in his settlement. I mean fine, I may not be able to craft mini-nukes at will, but the biggest advantage of an energy weapon in a post-apocalyptic world should be the ability to recharge it.

  2. The building system doesn't have enough parts that play well with uneven ground. You pretty much have to use concrete or stilts to get any kind of even platform to build on, but then those foundation blocks actually count as the floor of your building, so that means you can no longer make the outer walls from the premade pieces. You should be able to simply snap concrete or earthwork or stilts underneath whatever you've build to make it look nice and not have to worry so much about trying to make things snap just right.

  3. The poor implementation of sights in first person mode. Basically every major shooter uses a gun animation where the gun jerks back at the user, but keeps the sight center to the screen, the kick of the gun is simulated by nudging your camera up a little. In Fallout 4 the actual gun model kicks up, meaning your sights don't stay center to the screen, and all you can do is wait for them to settle. This kind of takes away your ability to compensate for recoil in first person mode. The worst part is, this doesn't happen in third person, there you just get an aim point that stays rock-steady dead center while the camera moves - the way it should be.
